core.headline: Travel Money & Payments · Spanish · Core
core.threshold: Use Spanish to complete the core travel money & payments conversations and explain the next step.

lessons.title: Exchange cash at a counter
lessons.objective: State the currencies and amount you want to exchange, then ask what net amount you will receive after the fee.
lessons.focus: Polite requests with quisiera and the question ¿cuánto recibo…? with a fixed fee subtracted from the converted amount.

words.note: The number of one currency given for another. Read it with the currency pair stated.
An amount charged for the service of exchanging money.
The amount that remains after fees or deductions have been taken away.
The currency of the United States and several other countries.
A paper note of money. The plural is billetes.
A written proof of the exchange, which you should check before you leave.
The currency used by many European countries. The plural is euros.
A shop or counter where you exchange one currency for another.
Does not change with the amount. Here it refers to a set fee.

words.es: Quisiera cambiar doscientos dólares a euros.
words.en: I would like to exchange two hundred dollars into euros.
words.note: A polite way to state the currency and amount at the start of an exchange.

words.en: How much do I receive in euros, net?
words.note: Asks for the final amount after all fees are taken away.
The formal command the clerk uses to ask for a signature.

words.es: Quiero revisar el recibo antes de irme.
words.en: I want to check the receipt before I leave.
words.note: Says you will verify the document before walking away.
A common closing wish from staff.

lessons.speaking: You stand at an exchange counter with two hundred US dollars. Say you want to exchange them into euros, ask what the net amount will be after the fee, and request two notes of a specific value. Close by checking the receipt and thanking the clerk.
lessons.partnerRole: Exchange-counter clerk who explains the rate and the fixed fee
lessons.openingLine: Buenas tardes. ¿Qué moneda quiere cambiar hoy y cuánto?

grammar.focus: Quisiera is a polite form of querer used to ask for something. Recibir takes the amount received as its object.

examples.es: Quisiera cambiar doscientos dólares a euros.
examples.en: I would like to exchange two hundred dollars into euros.

examples.es: ¿Cuánto recibo en euros, neto?
examples.en: How much do I receive in euros, net?

lessons.title: Read an exchange-rate quote
lessons.objective: Read a two-way exchange-rate board, identify which rate applies to buying or selling a currency, and say whether a fee is included.
lessons.focus: The preposition por to express a rate per unit, and the rate at which a currency is quoted.

words.note: The price of one currency in another. Always check the direction of the quote.
On a rate board, the buy rate: what the bank pays when it buys the currency from you.
On a rate board, the sell rate: what the bank charges when it sells the currency to you.
The display that shows the rate, the fee and the final amount.
One exchange of money, usually with its own fee.
An extra amount charged for the exchange service.
A currency used in several countries.
A man who works at a bank or service counter. The feminine form is empleada.
A number that represents an amount on a board or receipt.

words.en: What is the dollar rate today?
words.note: A natural question for the current price of a currency.

words.es: Si usted compra dólares, paga 0,95 euros por dólar.
words.en: If you buy dollars, you pay 0.95 euros per dollar.
words.note: Explains the rate that applies to a buyer.

words.es: ¿La comisión está incluida en ese precio?
words.en: Is the fee included in that price?
words.note: Confirms whether the amount shown is final.

words.en: It has to include the 2 euros.
words.note: A reminder that a fixed charge must be added to the total.

words.es: Puede confirmar la cifra en la pantalla.
words.en: You can confirm the figure on the screen.
words.note: A clerk's invitation to check the amount before you accept.

lessons.speaking: Ask a bank cashier the current dollar rate, then ask which figure applies if you buy dollars and which applies if you sell them. Ask whether a fee is included and confirm the final price shown on the screen before you decide.
lessons.partnerRole: Bank cashier who explains a rate board in simple terms
lessons.openingLine: Buenas tardes. ¿Quiere comprar o vender divisas hoy?

grammar.focus: Por expresses a rate per unit, as in 0,92 euros por dólar. Si usted compra dólares, paga… shows the price for a buyer with the verb pagar.

examples.es: Está a 0,92 euros por dólar.
examples.en: It is at 0.92 euros per dollar.

examples.es: Si usted compra dólares, paga 0,95 euros por dólar.
examples.en: If you buy dollars, you pay 0.95 euros per dollar.

lessons.title: Compare two exchange offers
lessons.objective: Compare two exchange offers that start with the same amount and identify which one gives a higher final amount in euros.
lessons.focus: Comparatives with más que, menos que and mejor que, plus sin comisión for an offer without a fee.

words.note: A proposal for an exchange or price, with stated terms.
Setting two amounts side by side to see which is larger.
The final amount after the rate and fee have been applied.
A charge added to an exchange; some offers list none.
A short word for the exchange rate in everyday talk.
The gap between two amounts or two rates.
An offer that does not charge a separate service fee.
The last amount after all adjustments have been made.
Less than the other amount or rate.

words.es: La oferta B es mejor que la oferta A.
words.en: Offer B is better than offer A.
words.note: Compares two offers to conclude which one suits you.

words.es: Con la oferta A recibo menos que con la B.
words.en: With offer A I receive less than with B.
words.note: Compares the final amount received under two options.

words.es: La comisión pesa más que la diferencia del tipo.
words.en: The fee outweighs the difference in the rate.
words.note: A clear explanation of why a small rate difference can lose value.

words.es: Quiero cambiar con la oferta B, por favor.
words.en: I want to exchange with offer B, please.
words.note: Confirms your decision in a polite request.

words.es: Tengo dos ofertas para cambiar doscientos dólares.
words.en: I have two offers to exchange two hundred dollars.
words.note: States the starting point for a comparison.

lessons.speaking: You hold two offers for the same two hundred dollars. Offer A has a rate of 0.92 and a five-euro fee. Offer B has a rate of 0.90 and no fee. Compare the final amounts aloud, decide which is better, and explain your choice. Close by asking the clerk to confirm the chosen one.
lessons.partnerRole: Exchange-office staff member who reads both offers with the traveler
lessons.openingLine: Buenas tardes. Tenemos dos ofertas para usted. ¿Le explico cada una?

grammar.focus: Más que and menos que compare amounts; mejor que is the irregular comparative of bueno. Aunque with a known fact takes the indicative: aunque el tipo es menor.

examples.es: La oferta B es mejor que la oferta A.
examples.en: Offer B is better than offer A.

examples.es: Con la oferta A recibo menos que con la oferta B.
examples.en: With offer A I receive less than with offer B.

lessons.title: Withdraw local currency at an ATM
lessons.objective: Ask a bank staff member about ATM fees and the withdrawal amount, and choose between local and home currency when the machine offers both.
lessons.focus: The indirect object me with cobrar, as in ¿me cobran…?, and por to name what a fee is for: por retirar, por cada retiro.

words.note: Taking money out of an account or an ATM.
A machine that gives cash from a bank account. Often shortened to cajero.
A charge for a service such as a withdrawal.
An extra amount added to a price, here built into the rate of the home-currency option.
Changing an amount from one currency into another, often done by a machine.
One act of taking money out of an account.
The group of ATMs or branches that a bank uses without an extra charge.
The currency used in the place you are visiting.
A printed proof of the transaction, showing the fee.
One choice that the machine or staff offers you.

words.es: ¿Me cobran comisión por retirar efectivo aquí?
words.en: Do they charge me a fee for withdrawing cash here?
words.note: Asks about fees before you make the withdrawal.

words.es: Si elige la moneda local, el cajero no hace la conversión.
words.en: If you choose the local currency, the ATM does not do the conversion.
words.note: Explains the cheaper option on a screen.

words.en: I want to withdraw one hundred euros.
words.note: States the amount for the transaction.

words.es: Pido el recibo con la comisión visible.
words.en: I ask for the receipt with the fee visible.
words.note: Requests proof that shows each charge.

words.es: El cajero se lo imprime al final.
words.en: The ATM will print it for you at the end.
words.note: Se lo: le becomes se before lo. Lo is the receipt.

lessons.speaking: You are at an ATM beside a bank branch. The machine offers to convert the withdrawal into your home currency. Ask the bank staff member whether there is a fee, which option costs less, and how much you will withdraw. Close by choosing the local currency and thanking them.
lessons.partnerRole: Bank staff member at a branch near an ATM who answers fee questions
lessons.openingLine: Buenos días. ¿Necesita ayuda con el cajero? Puedo explicarle las opciones.

grammar.focus: Me cobran uses the indirect object me with a plural verb to say they charge me. The fee is the direct object of cobrar.

examples.es: ¿Me cobran comisión por retirar?
examples.en: Do they charge me a fee for withdrawing?

examples.es: El cajero me cobra cinco euros.
examples.en: The machine charges me five euros.

lessons.title: Choose the currency for a card payment
lessons.objective: Choose the currency for a card payment, ask who converts the amount and which rate is quoted, and understand the charges shown before you approve.
lessons.focus: The subjunctive after recomendar que, as in compare, and the contrast between pagar en euros and pagar en dólares.

words.note: Changing an amount from one currency into another, done by the shop, the bank or the terminal.
The device that reads a card and asks for a confirmation.
A plastic payment card, such as a debit or credit card.
An amount added to a payment by a bank or service.
The institution that holds your account and issues your card.
The display that shows the amount and the currency.
The rate used to convert one currency into the other.
The type of money used for a payment.
The act of paying a price or bill.
A fixed amount charged for a service.

words.es: ¿Quién hace la conversión si pago con tarjeta?
words.en: Who makes the conversion if I pay by card?
words.note: A direct question about which party changes the currency.

words.es: ¿Qué tipo de cambio aplica la terminal?
words.en: Which exchange rate does the terminal apply?
words.note: Asks for the rate used in the card transaction.

words.en: I prefer to pay in euros.
words.note: Expresses your choice of currency with a reason implied.

words.es: Elijo euros y confirmo el pago.
words.en: I choose euros and confirm the payment.
words.note: Confirms the choice before the card is charged.

words.es: Le recomiendo que compare el tipo de la pantalla.
words.en: I recommend that you compare the rate on the screen.
words.note: Recomendar que is followed by a subjunctive: compare, not compara.

lessons.speaking: At a shop, the card terminal asks whether you want to pay in euros or in dollars. Ask who does the conversion, which rate the terminal uses, and whether the bank may charge a fee. Choose the currency you prefer and confirm it before the card is charged. Close by thanking the cashier.
lessons.partnerRole: Shop cashier who explains the card terminal's currency option
lessons.openingLine: Buenas tardes. Puede pasar la tarjeta cuando quiera. Primero la terminal le pregunta la moneda.

grammar.focus: After recomendar que, the next verb is subjunctive: que compare, que revise. Pagar en names the currency of the payment.

examples.es: Le recomiendo que compare el tipo de la pantalla.
examples.en: I recommend that you compare the rate on the screen.

examples.es: ¿Quién hace la conversión, la tienda o el banco?
examples.en: Who makes the conversion, the shop or the bank?

lessons.title: Manage cash denominations for a day
lessons.objective: Ask for smaller notes, divide a stated daily budget between planned purchases and say how much is left in plain words.
lessons.focus: Quantifiers poco, bastante, mucho and expressions más de and menos de with money amounts.

words.note: A planned amount of money for a day, trip or purchase.
A paper note of money; the plural billetes is used for several notes.
A ticket that lets you into a museum or show.
The meal eaten in the middle of the day; also the general word for food.
Something bought or given as a present.
Money in general, in notes, coins or account balances.
The part of an amount that remains after an expense is paid.
A payment made for something needed or wanted.
A public vehicle that travels along a fixed route.

words.es: Tengo un presupuesto de sesenta euros para hoy.
words.en: I have a budget of sixty euros for today.
words.note: States the planned amount for the day.

words.es: Me quedan más de treinta euros.
words.en: I have more than thirty euros left.
words.note: Describes the remaining money after several expenses.

words.es: Quiero cambiar este billete por billetes más pequeños.
words.en: I want to change this note into smaller notes.
words.note: A specific request for change with a clear purpose.

words.es: Tengo bastante dinero para un día tranquilo.
words.en: I have enough money for a calm day.
words.note: Confirms that the budget is sufficient.

words.es: Me quedan menos de treinta euros.
words.en: I have less than thirty euros left.
words.note: States an upper limit for the money that remains.

lessons.speaking: You have sixty euros in cash for the day. Plan a bus fare of two euros, a museum entry of twelve euros and a lunch of fifteen euros. Ask the clerk for smaller notes or coins for the bus, then subtract each planned expense aloud and say what is left. Close by confirming you have enough money for the day.
lessons.partnerRole: Clerk at a local bank branch who helps a traveler plan small payments
lessons.openingLine: Buenos días. ¿Quiere cambiar un billete grande por varios pequeños?

grammar.focus: Poco and bastante are quantifiers; más de and menos de come before a number, as in más de diez euros.

examples.es: Tengo bastante dinero para el día.
examples.en: I have enough money for the day.

examples.es: Me quedan menos de treinta euros.
examples.en: I have less than thirty euros left.

lessons.title: Pay for a taxi
lessons.objective: Confirm the fare basis, payment method and any extra charge with a taxi driver before you get in, and say which ones you accept.
lessons.focus: The preposition hasta for the end point of a trip, the question ¿cobra algún…? and the usted command suba.

words.note: The device in a taxi that shows the fare as the trip goes on.
The price charged for a trip, which may depend on distance and time.
An extra amount added to a fare, for example for luggage or night travel.
A case for clothes and personal items when you travel.
The place where planes take off and land.
The vehicles on the road, which can slow down a trip.
The starting fare shown on the meter before the trip begins.
Money in notes and coins, not a card.
A plastic payment card.

words.en: How much does it cost to go to the airport?
words.note: Asks the total for a named destination before you get in.

words.en: Do you charge any supplement for the suitcases?
words.note: Checks an extra cost before the trip starts.

words.es: ¿Puedo pagar con tarjeta, o solo en efectivo?
words.en: Can I pay by card, or only in cash?
words.note: Asks which payment method is accepted in the vehicle.

words.es: Entonces lo confirmo antes de subir.
words.en: Then I confirm it before getting in.
words.note: Settles the price in words before the trip begins.

words.es: Suba, por favor, que tengo prisa.
words.en: Get in, please, I am in a hurry.
words.note: A driver's request that starts the ride.

lessons.speaking: You are at a taxi rank with two large suitcases and need to go to the airport. Ask the total cost, ask whether there is a luggage supplement, and confirm whether you can pay by card. Decide whether to accept the extra and say so before you get in. Close by thanking the driver and asking them to start the trip.
lessons.partnerRole: Licensed taxi driver at a city rank who explains the meter and extras
lessons.openingLine: Buenas noches. ¿A dónde va? Suba, que tengo el motor encendido.

grammar.focus: Hasta marks the end of a trip; ir hasta is followed by a place. The usted command of -ir verbs ends in -a: subir gives suba.

examples.es: ¿Cuánto cuesta ir hasta el aeropuerto?
examples.en: How much does it cost to go to the airport?

examples.es: Suba, por favor, que tengo prisa.
examples.en: Get in, please, I am in a hurry.

lessons.title: Ask about a taxi fare difference
lessons.objective: Compare the agreed fare with the amount requested at arrival, ask for an itemized receipt and state clearly which amount you will pay.
lessons.focus: Acordamos as preterite, más de lo acordado for an excess over an agreed amount, and marcar for what a meter shows.

words.note: The device that shows the fare during the journey.
A price or condition that both parties have accepted in advance.
A written record of what was charged.
An extra cost added to the fare, such as a night charge.
The gap between the agreed amount and the requested amount.
The list that separates each charge in a bill or receipt.
The route you travel from start to end.
The sum of money requested for a service.
A formal request to correct a charge you believe is wrong.

words.en: We agreed on eighteen euros, right?
words.note: Restates the agreed price to check the other person's memory.

words.en: Do you charge a night supplement?
words.note: Asks about an extra charge before paying.

words.es: Quiero el recibo con el desglose.
words.en: I want the receipt with the breakdown.
words.note: Requests each part of the total in writing.

words.es: Son seis euros más de lo acordado.
words.en: It is six euros more than what we agreed.
words.note: Points out the exact difference in the amount.

words.es: Pago, guardo el recibo y reclamo la diferencia después.
words.en: I will pay, keep the receipt and claim the difference later.
words.note: Closes the payment with a clear plan for the disputed amount.

lessons.speaking: You agreed a fare of eighteen euros, but at arrival the driver asks for more because of the traffic. Ask why the amount is different, ask the meter reading, and request a receipt with each charge. State which amount you will pay now, keep the receipt and close by saying you will claim the six-euro difference later.
lessons.partnerRole: Taxi driver who asks for a higher fare at arrival and explains the extra charge
lessons.openingLine: Ya llegamos. Son veinticuatro euros, con el suplemento de noche.

grammar.focus: Acordamos is both present and preterite; context shows the past. Before lo acordado or a number, Spanish uses más de, not más que.

examples.es: Acordamos dieciocho euros, ¿verdad?
examples.en: We agreed eighteen euros, right?

examples.es: El taxímetro marcaba diecinueve euros.
examples.en: The meter showed nineteen euros.

lessons.title: Pay through a ride-hailing app
lessons.objective: Identify the amount already charged in a ride-hailing app, ask whether any cash payment is still needed, and decide how to add a tip.
lessons.focus: The adverbs ya and todavía for asking whether an action is already done or still pending.

words.note: A program on a phone that books and pays for the ride.
The person who drives the vehicle. The feminine form is conductora.
An extra amount given to say thanks for service. It is not required in every place.
The amount charged for the journey.
A proof of the payment, in paper or on a phone.
Money in notes and coins.
A mobile device used to order rides and show receipts.
A journey from a starting place to a destination.
Describes a charge that has already been settled.

words.es: ¿El viaje ya está pagado en la aplicación?
words.en: Is the trip already paid in the app?
words.note: Checks whether the app has settled the fare.

words.es: ¿Todavía tengo que pagar algo en efectivo?
words.en: Do I still have to pay anything in cash?
words.note: Asks about any amount still owed after the app payment.

words.es: Puede dar la propina en la aplicación.
words.en: You can give the tip in the app.
words.note: Explains a tip option without requiring it.

words.es: Ya tengo el recibo en el teléfono.
words.en: I already have the receipt on my phone.
words.note: Confirms the closing point of the transaction.
A driver's request that begins the ride.

lessons.speaking: You order a ride through an app and the driver arrives. Ask whether the trip is already paid in the app, ask whether you still have to pay anything in cash, and ask how a tip is added. Close by confirming that you have the receipt on your phone.
lessons.partnerRole: Ride-hailing driver who handles the app payment and a tip question
lessons.openingLine: Buenas tardes. ¿Es usted la señora de la aplicación? Suba, por favor.

grammar.focus: Ya means already and todavía means still. Ya pagué uses the past form to state that an action is complete.

examples.es: ¿Todavía tengo que pagar algo en efectivo?
examples.en: Do I still have to pay anything in cash?

examples.es: Ya pagué el viaje en la aplicación.
examples.en: I already paid for the trip in the app.

lessons.title: Buy public-transport tickets
lessons.objective: Ask the fare, number of journeys, validity and final price of a transport ticket before paying, and understand the terms printed on the ticket.
lessons.focus: The verb ofrecer and the preposition durante for a period of time, with plural agreement for several trips.

words.note: A paper or card ticket that allows a journey or set of journeys.
One trip on the metro, bus or train.
The period in which a ticket can be used.
An amount paid in advance and returned when the card is handed back.
Adding money or journeys to a card.
The counter where tickets are sold.
An underground railway in a city.
The total to pay. Ask whether a card deposit is added on top.
A ticket for one journey.

words.en: How many journeys does the ten-trip one include?
words.note: Asks the number of journeys in a bundle.

words.es: El billete es válido durante un año.
words.en: The ticket is valid for one year.
words.note: States the period in which the ticket works.

words.es: Son 20,50 euros, y el depósito es de 1 euro.
words.en: It is 20.50 euros, and the deposit is 1 euro.
words.note: Gives the fare and the deposit separately before the total.

words.en: So I pay 21.50 euros in total.
words.note: Confirms the total that includes the deposit.

words.es: Guardo el billete hasta que se acabe.
words.en: I keep the ticket until it runs out.
words.note: Closes the purchase with a plan for using the ticket.

lessons.speaking: You stand at a metro ticket office and want a multi-trip ticket. Ask which options are offered, how many journeys the ten-trip ticket includes, how long it is valid and the final price with the card deposit. Choose an option and confirm the total before paying. Close by saying you will keep the ticket until it runs out.
lessons.partnerRole: Ticket office clerk at an urban metro station who explains the fare options
lessons.openingLine: Buenos días. ¿Qué billete necesita? Tenemos sencillos y bonos de viajes.

grammar.focus: Durante is followed by a period of time: durante un año. Ofrecer adds z in the yo form (ofrezco); incluir adds y (incluyo, incluye).

examples.es: ¿Cuántos viajes incluye el de diez?
examples.en: How many journeys does the ten-trip one include?

examples.es: El billete es válido durante un año.
examples.en: The ticket is valid for one year.

lessons.title: Pay for a hotel stay
lessons.objective: Confirm the hotel total, currency, included services and the timing of payment, including whether you pay on arrival or on departure.
lessons.focus: Al with an infinitive to express the moment of an action, as in al llegar and al salir, and the verb salir in the present.

words.note: A booking made in advance for a room or a seat.
A person who stays at a hotel or is invited to a place.
The first meal of the day, sometimes included in the room rate.
The period of time you spend in a place.
The place in a hotel where guests check in and pay.
One night of a hotel stay.
The final amount for the stay.
An amount added for service or a specific item.
A document that lists what you owe for a stay or purchase.
Checks whether a meal is part of the room price.

words.es: ¿Se paga al llegar o al salir?
words.en: Do you pay on arrival or on departure?
words.note: Asks when the payment is due.

words.es: Puede pagar al salir, con tarjeta o en efectivo.
words.en: You can pay on departure, by card or in cash.
words.note: States the payment timing and methods allowed.

words.es: Todo está en euros y los cargos ya están dentro del precio.
words.en: Everything is in euros and the charges are already included in the price.
words.note: Confirms the currency and the included charges.

words.es: Le preparo la factura para el jueves.
words.en: I will prepare the bill for Thursday.
words.note: Confirms that the bill will be ready for the departure day.

lessons.speaking: You arrive at a hotel to check in for three nights. Ask whether breakfast is included, whether the total is in euros, and when you pay: on arrival or at departure. Choose the timing and confirm the total with the receptionist. Close by thanking them and saying you will pay at the desk when you leave.
lessons.partnerRole: Hotel receptionist at a city hotel who explains room rates and payment timing
lessons.openingLine: Buenas tardes. ¿Tiene una reserva a nombre de Cruz?

grammar.focus: Al plus an infinitive means on or upon doing something, as in al llegar. Salir is irregular in the first person: salgo.

examples.es: ¿Se paga al llegar o al salir?
examples.en: Do you pay on arrival or on departure?

examples.es: Pago al salir, con tarjeta.
examples.en: I pay on departure, by card.

lessons.title: Understand a hotel deposit or card hold
lessons.objective: Understand a hotel deposit or card hold, ask whether money is charged or only reserved, and confirm when the hold may be released.
lessons.focus: The verb hacer and the difference between cobrar, a charge, and retener, a hold on available money.

words.note: An amount reserved on a card that is not yet charged.
A sum paid or reserved to cover possible costs or damage.
To free an amount that was held so it becomes available again.
The institution that issues your card and controls your money.
A plastic payment card used for holds and charges.
An amount actually taken from the account or card.
The sum of money being held or charged.
A room in a hotel for guests to stay in.
A hotel worker who welcomes guests and handles check-in.

words.es: ¿Me cobran el depósito o solo me retienen el dinero?
words.en: Do you charge me the deposit, or only hold the money?
words.note: Asks the key difference between a charge and a hold.
Asks when the reserved amount becomes available again.

words.es: Solo hacemos una retención en la tarjeta.
words.en: We only place a hold on the card.
words.note: States that money is reserved, not taken.

words.en: We release it when you leave.
words.note: Cuando plus subjunctive (salga) refers to a future moment.

words.es: ¿Me da por escrito la cantidad retenida?
words.en: Can you give me the amount held in writing?
words.note: Asks for written confirmation of the amount.

lessons.speaking: At check-in, the hotel asks for a card so it can place a hold on money for incidentals. Ask whether money is charged or only held, ask when the hold will be released, and request the amount in writing. Close by saying you will keep the paper and thanking the receptionist.
lessons.partnerRole: Hotel receptionist who explains card holds and deposits
lessons.openingLine: Buenas noches. Necesito una tarjeta para hacer una retención por posibles gastos de la habitación.

grammar.focus: Hacer means to make or do and is used in hacer una retención. Retener is irregular in the first person: retengo. The verb liberar means to release.

examples.es: ¿Me cobran el depósito o solo me retienen el dinero?
examples.en: Do you charge me the deposit, or do you only hold the money?

examples.es: Solo hacemos una retención en la tarjeta.
examples.en: We only place a hold on the card.

lessons.title: Check a hotel bill
lessons.objective: Match each room charge and listed extra against the booking, identify any item you did not use, and request an itemized explanation.
lessons.focus: The preterite to report what was charged or consumed, with first-person forms such as consumí and cobraron.

words.note: The list of charges for a hotel stay or a restaurant meal.
A detailed list of each charge in a bill.
A confirmed arrangement for a room or flight.
One night of a hotel stay.
A small fridge in a room with drinks and snacks charged when used.
An amount added to the bill.
A written bill that can be corrected or reissued.
Shows each item and time separately.
The hotel room you stayed in.

words.es: Mi reserva era de tres noches, pero me cobraron cuatro.
words.en: My booking was for three nights, but they charged me for four.
words.note: States the difference between the booking and the bill.

words.en: I did not consume anything from the minibar.
words.note: Denies an item clearly in the past.

words.es: Pido una cuenta detallada con la hora de cada cargo.
words.en: I would like a detailed bill with the time of each charge.
words.note: Requests a full breakdown.

words.es: Lo reviso y le doy una factura corregida.
words.en: I will check it and give you a corrected bill.
words.note: A staff reply that accepts the review.

words.es: Yo me fui el día trece.
words.note: Gives the date that proves the error.

lessons.speaking: At checkout you see three nights on the bill but four room charges, and a minibar item you did not use. Compare the bill with your booking, state which charges are wrong, and ask for an itemized explanation. Close by asking for a corrected bill and thanking the receptionist.
lessons.partnerRole: Hotel front-desk cashier who reviews the folio with a departing guest
lessons.openingLine: Buenos días. ¿Va a pagar la cuenta de la habitación hoy?

grammar.focus: The preterite reports what happened in the past. Consumí is the first-person preterite of consumir; cobraron is the third-person plural.

examples.es: No consumí nada del minibar.
examples.en: I did not consume anything from the minibar.

examples.es: Me cobraron cuatro noches.
examples.en: They charged me for four nights.

lessons.title: Pay for a rental car
lessons.objective: Ask about the price, deposit, card requirement and charges included in a rental-car quote before you sign the contract.
lessons.focus: Hay que with an infinitive to state a requirement, and the adjective incluido agreeing with the charge it describes.

words.note: The hire of a car or another item for a set time.
A road vehicle for carrying passengers.
Security for the rental, often a card hold released at the end. In Spain depósito also means fuel tank.
Cover against damage or loss, sold as an extra or included in the quote.
The petrol or diesel used by the car.
The written agreement that sets the rental terms.
A card that allows payment on credit; some deposits require it.
A staff member who handles the rental counter.
The amount quoted for the rental period.

words.es: ¿El combustible está incluido o tengo que devolver el coche lleno?
words.en: Is fuel included, or do I have to return the car full?
words.note: Compares two fuel terms before you sign.

words.es: El seguro básico está incluido en el precio.
words.en: The basic insurance is included in the price.
words.note: States which cover is already part of the quote.
States a condition of the rental.

words.en: Can I use a debit card?
words.note: Asks whether your card is accepted for the deposit.

words.es: ¿Me da una copia del contrato, por favor?
words.en: Can you give me a copy of the contract, please?
words.note: Requests written proof of the agreement.

lessons.speaking: You are at a car-rental desk and want a small car for three days. Ask whether the quote includes insurance and fuel, ask what deposit the company holds, and confirm which card you must use. Decide whether to sign and say so. Close by thanking the agent and asking for a copy of the contract.
lessons.partnerRole: Rental agent at an airport desk who explains the quote and contract
lessons.openingLine: Buenas tardes. ¿Tiene reserva para un coche pequeño de tres días?

grammar.focus: Hay que followed by an infinitive means one must do something. Incluido agrees in gender and number with the charge it describes.

examples.es: Hay que dejar un depósito en tarjeta de crédito.
examples.en: A credit-card deposit must be left.

examples.es: El seguro básico está incluido en el precio.
examples.en: The basic insurance is included in the price.

lessons.title: Discuss a rental fuel charge
lessons.objective: Compare the fuel terms stated in the rental with the amount on the return receipt, and ask for the basis of the fuel charge.
lessons.focus: Clauses with cuando and the preterite, showing what happened when the car was returned.

words.note: The petrol or diesel that the car uses.
The amount of fuel left in the tank.
The container that holds the fuel; also a deposit in another context.
The number or level shown on a gauge or meter.
An amount added to the rental bill.
The rules of the rental that both parties must follow.
A printed or digital proof of the return and the charges.
The act of bringing back a rented car.
A dial or screen that shows the fuel level.

words.es: Cuando devolví el coche, el depósito estaba lleno.
words.en: When I returned the car, the tank was full.
words.note: States the condition at the moment of return.

words.es: Las condiciones decían que había que devolver el coche lleno.
words.en: The terms said the car had to be returned full.
words.note: Quotes the stated fuel requirement.

words.es: Muéstreme la lectura del medidor, por favor.
words.en: Please show me the gauge reading.
words.note: Asks for the evidence behind the fuel charge.

words.es: Debe quitar el cargo si el coche estaba lleno.
words.en: You must remove the charge if the car was full.
words.note: States the correction required.

words.es: Le doy un recibo corregido en un momento.
words.en: I will give you a corrected receipt in a moment.
words.note: A staff reply that accepts the correction.

lessons.speaking: You returned a rental car with a full tank, but the receipt shows a fuel charge. Describe when you returned the car and what the tank showed, then compare the stated fuel terms with the amount. Ask the agent to show the reading and to remove the charge if it is wrong. Close by asking for a corrected receipt.
lessons.partnerRole: Rental counter agent who checks the fuel gauge and the return receipt
lessons.openingLine: Buenos días. ¿Ha devuelto el coche hoy? Tengo que revisar el nivel de combustible.

grammar.focus: Cuando with the preterite introduces a completed action, as in cuando devolví. Devolví is the first-person preterite of devolver.

examples.es: Cuando devolví el coche, el depósito estaba lleno.
examples.en: When I returned the car, the tank was full.

examples.es: Cobraron combustible aunque el depósito estaba lleno.
examples.en: They charged for fuel although the tank was full.

lessons.title: Ask about a rental toll or parking fee
lessons.objective: Ask which provider charged a toll or parking fee, and whether an administrative charge is separate from the parking or toll itself.
lessons.focus: Relative clauses with que and lo que, as in el cargo que cobró la empresa, to identify which charge is meant.

words.note: A fee paid to use a road or motorway.
A place to leave a car, often charged by time.
A written message that informs you of a charge or problem.
A fee for processing a payment or a notice.
A road for fast traffic that often has tolls.
The work done to process a payment or document.
The sum shown on a notice or invoice.
A document listing each item or service charged.
Short for correo electrónico here; correo can also mean the postal service.

words.es: El peaje lo cobró la empresa de autopistas.
words.en: The toll was collected by the motorway company.
words.note: Identifies the provider that charged the fee.

words.es: ¿El cargo de gestión es aparte del peaje?
words.en: Is the handling charge separate from the toll?
words.note: Checks whether an administrative charge is a separate line.

words.es: Lo que cobran en total no coincide con el peaje.
words.en: What you charge in total does not match the toll.
words.note: Describes the mismatch in a precise way.

words.es: Pido el aviso por escrito, con cada cargo separado.
words.en: I would like the notice in writing, with each charge listed separately.
words.note: Requests an itemized document.

words.es: Se lo envío hoy mismo por correo electrónico.
words.en: I will send it to you by email today.
words.note: A staff reply that states the method and timing.

lessons.speaking: A rental company sends a notice about a toll and a parking charge. Ask which company charged the toll, whether the administration fee is separate from the amount, and what proof you can request. Decide whether to pay the notice or dispute it. Close by asking for the notice in writing.
lessons.partnerRole: Rental-company customer service agent who handles toll and parking notices
lessons.openingLine: Buenas tardes. Llamo por el aviso del peaje y el aparcamiento. ¿Qué necesita saber?

grammar.focus: Que introduces a relative clause that identifies a noun, as in el cargo que cobró la empresa. Lo que refers to a whole idea or amount.

examples.es: El cargo que cobró la empresa es un gasto de gestión.
examples.en: The charge that the company collected is an administrative expense.

examples.es: Lo que aparece en el aviso no coincide con el recibo.
examples.en: What appears on the notice does not match the receipt.

lessons.title: Pay a restaurant bill
lessons.objective: Confirm whether service charges and tips are included before paying a restaurant bill, and agree on the final amount you will pay.
lessons.focus: Estar with a past participle to describe a charge that is included, such as la propina está incluida.

words.note: The total amount of a restaurant meal, shown on paper or on screen.
Extra money given to a waiter to thank them for service.
A service charge included in the bill or the price.
A man who serves food and drinks in a restaurant.
A portion of food served on a plate.
A device at the table that reads a card for payment.
A printed or digital proof of the payment.
The final amount after all dishes and charges.
A container of drink, such as water or wine.

words.es: ¿La propina está incluida en la cuenta?
words.en: Is the tip included in the bill?
words.note: Checks whether a tip has already been added.

words.es: El servicio ya está incluido en el precio.
words.en: The service is already included in the price.
words.note: Says the service charge is part of the total.

words.es: Son treinta y cuatro euros con cincuenta céntimos.
words.en: It is thirty-four euros and fifty cents.
words.note: States the final total with cents.

words.en: I leave five euros as a tip.
words.note: States the tip amount clearly.

words.es: ¿Me puede traer el recibo cuando termine?
words.en: Can you bring me the receipt when you finish?
words.note: Asks for proof after the card payment.

lessons.speaking: At a restaurant table, the bill arrives. Ask whether service is included, confirm whether a tip is added, and check the final total before you pay by card. Close by thanking the waiter and asking for the receipt.
lessons.partnerRole: Waiter at a family restaurant who explains the bill and the service charge
lessons.openingLine: Buenas noches. ¿Ya terminaron? Les traigo la cuenta en un momento.

grammar.focus: Estar with a past participle shows the result of an action, as in el servicio está incluido. The participle agrees with the subject.

examples.es: ¿La propina está incluida en la cuenta?
examples.en: Is the tip included in the bill?

examples.es: El servicio ya está incluido en el precio.
examples.en: The service is already included in the price.

lessons.title: Split a bill
lessons.objective: Agree which items or what amount each person pays when splitting a bill, and decide whether separate receipts are needed.
lessons.focus: Cada uno as the subject of a singular verb, plus a medias and por separado for dividing a total.

words.note: The total amount due for a shared meal.
Divided into two equal parts between people.
In separate parts or in separate receipts.
The portion of the total that one person pays.
A portion of food served to one person.
A proof of payment for each person or group.
A container for wine or water.
An alcoholic drink made from grapes, often ordered as a shared bottle.
The full amount before the split.

words.en: Each person pays for their own dish.
words.note: States the split by item.

words.en: We split the cost of the wine equally.
words.note: Proposes an equal share of a shared item.

words.es: Pido recibo por separado, para mi empresa.
words.en: I would like a separate receipt for my company.
words.note: Asks for individual proof of payment.

words.es: Yo pago dieciséis, el precio de mi plato.
words.en: I pay sixteen, the price of my dish.
words.note: States one person's share and what it covers.

words.es: Entonces, cada uno paga su parte.
words.en: So each person pays their own share.
words.note: Summarizes the agreed split.

lessons.speaking: Three friends have a shared bill with a bottle of wine and three main dishes, but only two of them drink wine. Propose how to split it, agree on who pays for the shared wine, and ask whether separate receipts are possible. Close by confirming each person's share in euros.
lessons.partnerRole: Waiter at a tapas bar who asks how a group of three wants to pay
lessons.openingLine: Buenas noches. ¿Quieren pagar juntos o cada uno por separado?

grammar.focus: Cada uno takes a singular verb: cada uno paga. A medias means equally divided between two people. Por separado means individually.

examples.es: Cada uno paga su plato.
examples.en: Each person pays for their own dish.

examples.es: Pagamos el vino a medias.
examples.en: We split the cost of the wine equally.

lessons.title: Bargain at a market
lessons.objective: Ask for a better price at a market stall, clarify whether a price is per kilo or for the whole quantity, and decide whether to buy.
lessons.focus: The construction hacer un precio for a discount, and the difference between por kilo and en total.

words.note: A unit of weight used at markets; kilo is short for kilogramo.
A red fruit often sold by weight at a stall.
The amount asked for a product; regatear means to bargain for it.
A person who sells goods at a stall.
How good the product is, which you can check before buying.
The whole amount for all the items together.
A small place in a market where goods are sold.
The time of year when a product is at its best or cheapest.
The smaller unit of the euro.

words.es: ¿Me hace un precio si compro tres kilos?
words.en: Can you give me a better price if I buy three kilos?
words.note: Asks for a lower price linked to a larger quantity.

words.es: ¿Ese precio es por kilo o en total?
words.en: Is that price per kilo or in total?
words.note: Clears up the unit before you agree.

words.es: Lo pienso un momento antes de decidir.
words.en: I will think about it for a moment before I decide.
words.note: Gives time without refusing the offer.

words.en: Then I will take two kilos.
words.note: Confirms the quantity you have chosen.
Checks the total before paying.

lessons.speaking: You are at a fruit stall and want two or three kilos of tomatoes. Ask the price per kilo, ask whether the vendor can give you a better price for three kilos, and confirm whether the total is per kilo or for all of them. Decide how many kilos you buy and close by paying in coins.
lessons.partnerRole: Fruit and vegetable vendor at a Spanish-speaking market who negotiates prices
lessons.openingLine: Buenos días, joven. Hoy los tomates están muy buenos, a precio de temporada.

grammar.focus: Hacer un precio means to offer a reduced price. Por kilo states a unit price, while en total states the full amount.

examples.es: ¿Me hace un precio si compro tres kilos?
examples.en: Can you give me a better price if I buy three kilos?

examples.es: ¿Ese precio es por kilo o en total?
examples.en: Is that price per kilo or in total?

lessons.title: Compare a cash price and a card price
lessons.objective: Ask why the card price is higher than the cash price, confirm the final amount before choosing a method, and state which one you prefer.
lessons.focus: Por qué as a question about a reason and porque as the answer that gives the reason.

words.note: An extra amount added to the regular price. A cash discount reduces the regular price; ask for the final total.
The amount asked for an item.
Money in notes and coins.
A plastic payment card.
A piece of clothing worn over other clothes.
A worker who serves customers in a shop. The feminine form is dependienta.
The gap between two prices.
To keep money by paying less than expected.
The price after every charge and surcharge is included.

words.es: ¿Por qué el precio con tarjeta es más alto?
words.en: Why is the price with a card higher?
words.note: Asks the reason for two different prices.

words.es: Porque en efectivo le hacemos un descuento de tres euros.
words.en: Because we give you a three-euro discount for cash.
words.note: Porque introduces the answer; por qué asks the question.

words.es: ¿Me confirma el precio final antes de pagar?
words.en: Can you confirm the final price before I pay?
words.note: Asks for confirmation before choosing the method.

words.es: Prefiero pagar en efectivo y ahorrar tres euros.
words.en: I prefer to pay in cash and save three euros.
words.note: States the payment choice and the saving.

words.es: Con tarjeta son cuarenta y cinco euros.
words.en: By card it is forty-five euros.
words.note: Gives the card total for comparison.

lessons.speaking: At a clothing shop, the card price on a jacket is forty-five euros, while the cash price is forty-two. Ask why the card price is higher, confirm the final amount with the cashier, and choose a payment method. Close by saying you prefer to pay in cash and saving the difference.
lessons.partnerRole: Shop assistant at a clothing store who explains a cash discount
lessons.openingLine: Buenas tardes. ¿Le ayudo con la chaqueta? Tiene un precio especial en efectivo.

grammar.focus: Por qué asks for a reason; porque gives the reason. Más barato and más caro compare two prices.

examples.es: ¿Por qué el precio con tarjeta es más alto?
examples.en: Why is the price with a card higher?

examples.es: Porque el pago en efectivo tiene un descuento.
examples.en: Because the cash payment has a discount.

lessons.title: Pay a booking deposit
lessons.objective: Confirm the booking deposit, the remaining balance, the due date and the written cancellation terms before paying anything.
lessons.focus: Antes del and hasta el with dates, plus the reflexive passive se devuelve for what is returned.

words.note: An amount paid in advance to secure a booking. In Spain a booking deposit is also called la señal.
The remaining amount still to be paid after the deposit.
A confirmed arrangement for accommodation.
The act of ending a booking before the stay.
The last date by which something must be done.
The written terms that set what is allowed.
Sending money from one account to another.
A written paper or file that records terms or payments.
A self-contained flat for holiday stays.

words.en: When do I have to pay the balance?
words.note: Asks the due date for the remaining amount.

words.es: Puede cancelar hasta el 1 de diciembre.
words.note: States the last date for cancellation.

words.es: Lo quiero por escrito, por favor.
words.en: I want it in writing, please.
words.note: Asks for the terms as a written document.

words.es: Le envío el documento con las condiciones por correo.
words.en: I will send you the document with the conditions by email.
words.note: A staff reply that confirms the written terms.

lessons.speaking: You are booking a holiday apartment by email and need to pay a deposit now. Ask the deposit amount and the balance, ask the due date for the balance, and ask until which date you can cancel and get the deposit back. Confirm that you will pay the deposit today and ask for the terms in writing. Close by thanking the staff member.
lessons.partnerRole: Holiday-apartment reservations clerk who sends a written booking summary
lessons.openingLine: Buenas tardes, gracias por escribirnos. ¿Quiere confirmar la reserva del apartamento?

grammar.focus: Antes del marks the date before which something must happen. Se devuelve is a reflexive passive used when a sum is given back.

examples.es: El saldo se paga antes del 10 de diciembre.
examples.en: The balance is paid before 10 December.

examples.es: Puede cancelar hasta el 1 de diciembre.
examples.en: You can cancel until 1 December.

lessons.title: Ask about a refund
lessons.objective: State what you paid, ask the refund terms for a cancelled tour, and find out how and when the money is returned.
lessons.focus: The reflexive passive ¿cómo se devuelve…?, and the future tense devolveremos for a promised timeline.

words.note: Money returned to the payer after a cancellation or change.
The act of giving money back.
The written rules a company applies to cancellations and payments.
How early you cancel before the start of a service.
A company that books tours, flights and holidays.
A trip that you take for a day, often with a guide.
A confirmed arrangement for a tour, room or flight.
The rules that you agree to when you book.
Electronic mail used to confirm a refund.

words.en: Do they return the money if I cancel?
words.note: Asks if a refund is due.
Asks the method of refund.

words.es: Se devuelve el 80 por ciento si cancela con siete días.
words.en: 80 percent is returned if you cancel seven days ahead.
words.note: Explains the percentage and the timing rule.

words.es: Se lo devolveremos en cinco días hábiles.
words.en: We will return it to you in five business days.
words.note: States the timing promised by the agency.

words.en: I want to confirm it by email.
words.note: Asks for written confirmation of the refund.

lessons.speaking: You booked a day tour for one hundred euros and cancelled nine days ahead. Explain what you paid, ask whether the money is returned, and confirm the percentage and timing. Ask whether the refund goes back to the card. Close by saying you will confirm by email.
lessons.partnerRole: Travel agency clerk who handles cancellations and refunds
lessons.openingLine: Buenas tardes. ¿Me puede dar el número de su reserva? Lo busco ahora.

grammar.focus: ¿Cómo se devuelve? uses se with a third-person verb for an unnamed process. Devolveremos is the future form of devolver for a promised timing.

examples.es: ¿Cómo se devuelve el dinero?
examples.en: How is the money returned?

examples.es: Se lo devolveremos en cinco días hábiles.
examples.en: We will return it to you in five business days.

lessons.title: Make a refundable reservation
lessons.objective: Distinguish the booking price from a refundable option and request the exact written terms, including the cancellation deadline.
lessons.focus: The present subjunctive in a relative clause describing a wanted option, as in una tarifa que se pueda cancelar.

words.note: A rate that allows changes or cancellations, usually for a higher price.
A lower rate that often does not allow a refund.
Money returned after a cancellation.
The rules of the booking written in the confirmation.
A confirmed arrangement for a room or a flight.
The day or time when a guest or traveler arrives.
An amount charged to a card or account.
One night of a room stay.
A written proof that the booking is confirmed.

words.es: Quiero una tarifa que se pueda cancelar.
words.en: I want a rate that can be cancelled.
words.note: States the requirement clearly.

words.es: ¿La tarifa básica no se puede cancelar?
words.en: The basic rate cannot be cancelled?
words.note: Checks the cancellation rule of the cheaper option.

words.es: ¿Me envía las condiciones exactas por escrito?
words.en: Can you send me the exact terms in writing?
words.note: Requests the written terms before choosing.

words.es: Puede cancelar hasta el día antes de la llegada.
words.en: You can cancel until the day before arrival.
words.note: States the deadline for cancelling without a charge.

words.en: Then I want the flexible rate.
words.note: Makes the decision after comparing both options.

lessons.speaking: You phone a hotel reservations centre and want a room that can be cancelled. Ask whether the flexible rate costs more than the basic rate, ask whether the basic rate can be cancelled, and request the exact terms in writing. Choose the option you want and confirm the deadline. Close by thanking the agent and ending the call.
lessons.partnerRole: Hotel reservations agent on the phone who explains flexible and basic rates
lessons.openingLine: Buenos días, central de reservas. ¿En qué le puedo ayudar?

grammar.focus: Que se pueda cancelar uses the present subjunctive of poder because the speaker describes the kind of rate wanted rather than a known one. Admitir means to allow.

examples.es: Quiero una tarifa que se pueda cancelar.
examples.en: I want a rate that can be cancelled.

examples.es: La tarifa básica no admite devolución.
examples.en: The basic rate does not allow a refund.

lessons.title: Change a travel booking
lessons.objective: Compare the new price, the change fee and any remaining credit when changing a travel booking, and calculate what you would pay.
lessons.focus: The conditional pagaría for a hypothetical result after si plus imperfect subjunctive (si cambiara), contrasted with si plus present for a real plan.

words.note: A fee for altering a booking. Avoid tasa de cambio here: in much of Latin America it means exchange rate.
An amount kept from an earlier booking that can be used later.
The extra amount between the old and the new booking.
The booking that is being changed.
The day of travel or stay.
The full amount to be paid after the fee and credit.
Altering a booking, or the money given back in a shop.
A single action that is charged.
The amount asked for the trip.

words.es: Si cambiara la fecha, ¿cuánto pagaría en total?
words.en: If I changed the date, how much would I pay in total?
words.note: Asks the total for a hypothetical change.

words.es: ¿Me queda algún crédito de la reserva anterior?
words.en: Is there any credit left from the previous booking?
words.note: Asks whether an old amount can be used.

words.es: Son 85 euros en total, con el cargo incluido.
words.en: It is 85 euros in total, with the fee included.
words.note: States the full sum including the change fee.

words.es: Entonces, con el crédito, pagaría 70 euros.
words.en: So, with the credit, I would pay 70 euros.
words.note: Calculates the net amount with the credit.
A polite instruction to proceed with the change.

lessons.speaking: You want to move your booked trip by a week. Ask the change fee, ask what the total would be, and ask whether any credit from the old booking remains. Calculate the net amount you would pay after using the credit, and decide whether to make the change. Close by asking the agent to make the change now.
lessons.partnerRole: Travel-booking change agent who explains fees, price differences and credit
lessons.openingLine: Buenos días. Dígame, ¿qué quiere cambiar en su reserva de viaje?

grammar.focus: Pagaría is the conditional of pagar. A hypothetical si clause takes the imperfect subjunctive: si cambiara. A real plan uses si plus present: si cambio, pago.

examples.es: Si cambiara la fecha, ¿cuánto pagaría en total?
examples.en: If I changed the date, how much would I pay in total?

examples.es: Si cambio la fecha hoy, pago 70 euros con el crédito.
examples.en: If I change the date today, I pay 70 euros with the credit.

lessons.title: Purchase a tour or attraction ticket
lessons.objective: Ask which costs are included in a tour or attraction ticket, identify what must be paid separately on arrival, and buy the right combination.
lessons.focus: Tener que with an infinitive to state an obligation, and the object pronoun attached to the infinitive in Tiene que pagarla.

words.note: The standard ticket that gives access without a guide.
A tour led by a guide who explains the place.
The counter where tickets are sold and paid.
A tall building or structure that visitors can climb.
The level at street height, where the entrance usually is.
Not included in the price; paid as its own item.
Part of the price already counted in the total.
The sum of all tickets and options chosen.

words.es: ¿La visita guiada está incluida en la entrada?
words.en: Is the guided visit included in the entry?
words.note: Checks whether a second item is part of the first price.

words.es: Tiene que pagarla aparte, en la taquilla.
words.en: You must pay for it separately, at the counter.
words.note: States the required separate payment and where to make it.
Confirms the sum before paying.
A staff phrase when handing over a ticket.

lessons.speaking: At the ticket counter of a tower, ask the general entry price and the guided visit price, ask whether the guided visit is included, and say where the separate payment is made. Confirm the total and say you will go up after you pay. Close by thanking the clerk and asking the start time.
lessons.partnerRole: Ticket clerk at a historic tower with a guided visit option
lessons.openingLine: Buenas tardes. ¿Entrada general o con visita guiada hoy?

grammar.focus: Tener que plus an infinitive means must do something. In Tiene que pagarla the pronoun la attaches to the infinitive and refers to la visita.

examples.es: Tiene que pagar la visita aparte.
examples.en: You must pay for the visit separately.

examples.es: Pagarla en taquilla es lo más rápido.
examples.en: Paying for it at the ticket office is the quickest.

lessons.title: Pay for laundry or another local service
lessons.objective: Compare a per-item laundry price with a per-kilo price, understand what each one includes, and agree on a pick-up time.
lessons.focus: The preposition por for a unit of measure in prices (por kilo, por prenda), and the future tense for an agreed pick-up.

words.note: A shop or service that washes clothes for customers.
One piece of clothing counted separately in a price.
A unit of weight used to price laundry by weight.
The step that dries clothes, sometimes included in the price.
Pressing clothes with an iron; sometimes charged as a separate service.
Garments collected for washing.
A garment with buttons worn on the upper body.
A garment covering the legs, counted as one item.
The time around twelve o'clock when a pick-up is often set.

words.es: ¿Cómo cobran el lavado de la ropa?
words.en: How do you charge for washing clothes?
words.note: Asks how the service is priced before you commit.

words.en: How much would it be per item?
words.note: Asks the price for one item unit.

words.es: Por kilo son dos euros con cincuenta.
words.en: By the kilo it is two euros fifty.
words.note: States the price by weight.

words.es: Entonces por kilo me conviene más.
words.en: Then by the kilo suits me better.
words.note: Chooses the cheaper unit for your load.

words.en: You will pay when you collect it.
words.note: States the payment time for the laundry.

lessons.speaking: You have a bag of shirts and trousers to wash at a laundry. Ask how the laundry charges, compare the per-item price with the per-kilo price, and decide which is cheaper. Ask whether it is ready tomorrow and when you pay. Close by confirming the pick-up time.
lessons.partnerRole: Laundry manager who explains the prices by item or by weight
lessons.openingLine: Buenos días. ¿Trae la ropa para lavar, planchar o solo para el secado?

grammar.focus: Por expresses the unit of a price: por kilo or por prenda. Pagará is the future tense of pagar, used for a planned payment.

examples.es: Cobramos por kilo o por prenda.
examples.en: We charge by the kilo or by the item.

examples.es: Pagará al recogerla.
examples.en: You will pay when you collect it.

lessons.title: Send or receive travel money
lessons.objective: Confirm the recipient, payout amount, fee, currency and expected availability before sending money to someone abroad.
lessons.focus: The future tense for expected arrival and availability, and the verb descontar for a fee taken from the amount.

words.note: The person who receives the money sent.
Sending money from one account or service to another.
The amount charged for sending the transfer.
The sum of money being sent or paid.
The type of money in which the recipient is paid.
Ready to use or collect at a given time.
A proof that the transfer was made.
The rate used to convert the amount into the other currency.
The bank where the recipient's account is held.

words.en: How much will she receive in her currency?
words.note: Asks the payout in the local currency.

words.es: ¿Cuándo estará disponible el dinero para ella?
words.en: When will the money be available for her?
words.note: Asks for the expected timing.

words.es: La comisión se descuenta de los 300 euros.
words.en: The fee is deducted from the 300 euros.
words.note: The fee comes out of the amount sent, so less is converted.

words.es: Confirme el nombre del destinatario, por favor.
words.note: Checks the person receiving the money.

words.es: Guardo el comprobante de la transferencia.
words.note: States that you keep the proof of the transfer.

lessons.speaking: You want to send three hundred euros to a relative in another country. Ask how much the recipient will receive in the local currency, when the money will be available, and whether the fee is taken from the amount. Confirm the recipient's name and ask for a receipt of the transfer. Close by saying you will keep the receipt.
lessons.partnerRole: Money transfer agent at a service counter who explains fees and payout times
lessons.openingLine: Buenas tardes. ¿Desea enviar dinero al extranjero hoy?

grammar.focus: The future recibirá, estará and llegará describes what is expected. Se descuenta is passive se: the fee is taken off the sum.

examples.es: Recibirá 316,80 dólares con el tipo de hoy.
examples.en: She will receive 316.80 dollars at today's rate.

examples.es: La comisión se descuenta del importe.
examples.en: The fee is deducted from the amount.

lessons.title: Keep a daily travel-money record
lessons.objective: Keep a simple daily travel-money record that shows what was paid, what remains available and which expenses are still pending.
lessons.focus: The present perfect with haber plus a past participle, as in he pagado, for expenses completed today.

words.note: A written list of payments and balances kept during a trip.
A payment made for something during the trip.
Not yet paid or settled.
The midday meal.
An amount paid in advance as security.
Money not yet committed to any payment.
The sum of all the expenses added together.
A ticket that gives access to a place such as a museum.
A railway vehicle used for travel between towns.

words.es: He pagado el tren y el almuerzo.
words.en: I have paid for the train and the lunch.
words.note: Records completed payments in the present perfect.

words.en: How much have you spent in total?
words.note: Asks the total spent so far.

words.es: El depósito del hotel aún no está pagado.
words.en: The hotel deposit is not yet paid.
words.note: States a pending amount clearly.
Gives the amount left after pending items.

words.es: Lo apunto todo en el registro del viaje.
words.en: I write it all in the travel record.
words.note: Closes the review with a record.

lessons.speaking: With a travel companion, review the day's payments aloud. Say which expenses you have already paid, say the total spent, and identify any amount still pending. Calculate what you have left as free money. Close by saying you will write it in the travel record.
lessons.partnerRole: Travel companion who asks about the day's payments
lessons.openingLine: ¿Qué tal el día? ¿Has pagado ya todos los gastos de hoy?

grammar.focus: He pagado uses haber in the present plus a past participle for an action completed in the recent past. Pending expenses use aún no or todavía no.

examples.es: He pagado el tren y el almuerzo.
examples.en: I have paid for the train and the lunch.

examples.es: El depósito del hotel aún no está pagado.
examples.en: The hotel deposit is not yet paid.

lessons.title: Ask about a local visitor tax
lessons.objective: Ask what a local visitor tax is, who collects it, how often it is charged and what receipt you receive, while noting that rates and names differ by place.
lessons.focus: Passive se agreeing with its noun (se cobra una tasa, se cobran dos euros) and quien after a comma for a person.

words.note: In Spain some regions or city councils charge visitors per night; name, rate and rules vary. Amounts here are fictional.
A place to stay, such as a hotel, hostel or apartment.
The local government of a town or city.
An individual who stays at the place and is counted for the tax.
The highest number or amount allowed.
A written proof of payment for the tax and other charges.
One night of a stay.
The total amount due at check-out.
The price or amount set for a service or tax.

words.en: How much is the tax per night?
words.note: Asks the amount per night in the local area.

words.es: Se cobra por persona y por noche.
words.en: It is charged per person and per night.
words.note: Explains how the tax is calculated.
Asks which party receives the money.

words.es: La pago al salir, junto con la cuenta.
words.en: I pay it at check-out, together with the bill.
words.note: States the timing of payment.

words.es: Le daré un recibo que indique la tasa por separado.
words.en: I will give you a receipt that shows the tax separately.
words.note: A staff promise to show the tax on its own line.

lessons.speaking: At the hotel desk, you hear about a local visitor tax you did not expect. Ask what it is called in this city, how much it is per night, who collects it, and when you pay. Ask for a receipt that shows the tax on its own line. Close by agreeing to pay it at check-out.
lessons.partnerRole: Hotel receptionist who explains a city's local visitor tax without giving universal rules
lessons.openingLine: Buenas noches. ¿Tiene alguna pregunta sobre su estancia o los cargos locales?

grammar.focus: Passive se agrees with the noun: se cobra una tasa, se cobran dos euros. Quien introduces a person after a comma: la recepcionista, quien explica.

examples.es: En esta ciudad se cobra una tasa por persona y por noche.
examples.en: In this city a tax is charged per person and per night.

examples.es: La recepcionista, quien conoce las tarifas, me lo explica.
examples.en: The receptionist, who knows the rates, explains it to me.

lessons.title: Complete a routine travel-payment day
lessons.objective: Describe a full day of travel payments: cash for transport, an itemized meal, a hotel hold, an agreed taxi fare and the cash left for tomorrow.
lessons.focus: Mixing the preterite for completed actions, the imperfect for a past situation, and the present for a current balance.

words.note: Small metal pieces of money used for bus fares and small payments.
A fixed-price meal offered at midday in many restaurants.
Extra money given to say thanks for service.
To keep an amount on a card without taking it yet.
The device that shows the fare during a taxi journey.
A fare both sides accepted before the trip.
A written proof of the payment, kept to claim later.
Money in notes and coins.
To ask for money or a correction back after a payment.

words.en: I paid for the bus with coins.
words.note: Records a completed cash payment.
States the amount and method of a meal payment.

words.es: La recepcionista me dijo que retendrían 120 euros.
words.en: The receptionist told me they would hold 120 euros.
words.note: Reports a hold using the conditional tense.

words.es: Le pedí que me explicara la diferencia.
words.en: I asked them to explain the difference.
words.note: Reports a request: pedir que plus the imperfect subjunctive explicara.

words.en: I have 35 euros in cash left.
words.note: Gives the balance for tomorrow.

words.es: Guardé el recibo para reclamar la diferencia.
words.en: I kept the receipt to claim the difference.
words.note: Records the proof needed for a later claim.

lessons.speaking: Tell a friend how you paid for each part of your day: the bus with coins, the meal by card with an itemized bill, the hotel hold and the taxi fare. Explain the difference you noticed and how you resolved it, then say how much cash you have for tomorrow. Close by asking your friend to check the record with you.
lessons.partnerRole: Friend who asks about the day's payments and checks the record with you
lessons.openingLine: ¿Cómo fue tu día con los pagos? Cuéntame cómo resolviste el taxi.

grammar.focus: The preterite gives completed actions, such as pagué; the imperfect gives an ongoing condition, such as marcaba; the present gives the current balance, such as me quedan.

examples.es: Pagué el autobús con monedas por la mañana.
examples.en: I paid for the bus with coins in the morning.

examples.es: El taxímetro marcaba once euros cuando llegamos.
examples.en: The meter was showing eleven euros when we arrived.

reading.title: En el mercado de la plaza
target: Turista: Buenos días. ¿Cuánto cuesta este melón?
Vendedora: El precio es de cuatro euros. Está muy dulce.
Turista: ¿Y cuánto cuestan dos limones?
Vendedora: Cada limón cuesta 1 euro.
Turista: ¿Cuánto es en total?
Vendedora: Son seis euros en total.
Turista: Perfecto. Me lo llevo todo, gracias.
native: Tourist: Good morning. How much does this melon cost?
Vendor: The price is four euros. It is very sweet.
Tourist: And how much do two lemons cost?
Vendor: Each lemon costs 1 euro.
Tourist: How much is it in total?
Vendor: It is six euros in total.
Tourist: Perfect. I will take it all, thank you.

1.speaking: You are buying fruit at a market stall. Ask the price of one melon and of two lemons, then repeat each amount back in euros. Close by saying the melon is the one you will take, and thank the vendor.
1.openingLine: Buenos días. ¿Qué le pongo hoy? Tenemos melones muy dulces.
1.partnerRole: Fruit vendor at a Spanish-speaking weekly market

grammar.focus: Price questions agree with the item: ¿Cuánto cuesta? for one thing, ¿Cuánto cuestan? for more than one.

examples.es: ¿Cuánto cuesta este melón?
examples.en: How much does this melon cost?

examples.es: ¿Cuánto cuestan estos limones?
examples.en: How much do these lemons cost?

reading.title: Precios con céntimos en la panadería
target: Cliente: ¿Cuánto cuesta el pan?
Panadero: El pan cuesta 2,50 euros: dos euros con cincuenta céntimos.
Cliente: ¿Y el agua?
Panadero: El agua cuesta 1,20 euros.
Cliente: Entonces, ¿el total es 3,70 euros?
Panadero: Exacto. Los céntimos van después de la coma.
Cliente: Entiendo. Pago con un billete de cinco euros.
Panadero: Perfecto. Le devuelvo un euro con treinta céntimos.
native: Customer: How much does the bread cost?
Baker: The bread costs 2.50 euros: two euros and fifty cents.
Customer: And the water?
Baker: The water costs 1.20 euros.
Customer: So, is the total 3.70 euros?
Baker: Exactly. The cents come after the comma.
Customer: I understand. I will pay with a five-euro note.
Baker: Perfect. I will give you back one euro and thirty cents.

2.speaking: You are buying bread and bottled water at a bakery counter. Say the price of each item in full, using euros and cents, then add them together and confirm the total with the baker.
2.openingLine: Buenas tardes. ¿Qué le sirvo? El pan de hoy está recién horneado.
2.partnerRole: Baker at a neighborhood bakery who checks each price aloud

grammar.focus: Spanish writes the decimal with a comma; céntimos are the cents, and cents follow the word con or y.

examples.es: El pan cuesta 2,50 euros.
examples.en: The bread costs 2.50 euros.

examples.es: Son dos euros con cincuenta céntimos.
examples.en: It is two euros and fifty cents.

reading.title: En el quiosco de la estación
target: Turista: Perdone, ¿cuánto vale esta moneda?
Dependienta: Es una moneda de dos euros.
Turista: ¿Y qué billete es este, el de diez euros?
Dependienta: No, este es un billete de cinco euros.
Turista: Necesito monedas de un euro para el autobús. ¿Tiene cambio de cinco euros?
Dependienta: Sí. Por su billete le doy tres monedas de un euro y una de dos.
Turista: Perfecto. Para el autobús son tres euros exactos, ¿verdad?
Dependienta: Sí, exacto. Gracias por su visita.
native: Tourist: Excuse me, how much is this coin worth?
Clerk: It is a two-euro coin.
Tourist: And which note is this, the ten-euro one?
Clerk: No, this is a five-euro note.
Tourist: I need one-euro coins for the bus. Do you have change for five euros?
Clerk: Yes. For your note I will give you three one-euro coins and one two-euro coin.
Tourist: Perfect. For the bus that is exactly three euros, right?
Clerk: Yes, exactly. Thank you for visiting.

3.speaking: You are at a newsstand with a five-euro note and only small coins. Ask what one coin is worth, then ask for the right number of one-euro coins for a bus fare of three euros, and confirm the total before you pay.
3.openingLine: Buenas tardes. ¿Qué necesita? Si quiere, le ayudo con el cambio.
3.partnerRole: Newsstand attendant who explains coins and notes calmly

grammar.focus: Un and una mark a single item; de plus the value gives a denomination, as in un billete de cinco euros.

examples.es: Tengo un billete de cinco euros.
examples.en: I have a five-euro note.

examples.es: Necesito unas monedas de un euro.
examples.en: I need some one-euro coins.

reading.title: ¿Efectivo o tarjeta?
target: Turista: Buenas tardes. ¿Aceptan tarjeta de crédito?
Camarero: Sí, aceptamos tarjeta para pagos de más de cinco euros.
Turista: ¿Y puedo pagar en efectivo si la cuenta es de cuatro euros?
Camarero: Claro, siempre aceptamos efectivo.
Turista: Entonces pago en efectivo, por favor.
Camarero: Perfecto. El café y el pastel cuestan cuatro euros.
Turista: Muy bien. Aquí tiene el dinero.
Camarero: Gracias. Le traigo el recibo ahora mismo.
native: Tourist: Good afternoon. Do you accept credit cards?
Waiter: Yes, we accept cards for payments over five euros.
Tourist: And can I pay in cash if the bill is four euros?
Waiter: Of course, we always accept cash.
Tourist: Then I will pay in cash, please.
Waiter: Perfect. The coffee and the cake cost four euros.
Tourist: Very well. Here is the money.
Waiter: Thank you. I will bring you the receipt right now.

4.speaking: You enter a café and want a coffee and a cake. Ask if the café accepts credit cards, ask whether cash is also accepted, then choose the method you will use and confirm the amount with the waiter.
4.openingLine: Buenas tardes. ¿Qué desea tomar? Tenemos café, té y pasteles.
4.partnerRole: Waiter at a busy café who accepts both cash and cards

grammar.focus: Yes/no questions can begin with the verb, as in ¿Aceptan tarjeta? Pagar con names the card or other method; pagar en efectivo means paying in cash.

examples.es: ¿Aceptan tarjeta de crédito aquí?
examples.en: Do you accept credit cards here?

examples.es: ¿Puedo pagar en efectivo?
examples.en: Can I pay in cash?

reading.title: Un billete grande en la tienda
target: Cliente: Buenas noches. Quisiera un zumo, por favor.
Dependiente: Muy bien. Son dos euros con cincuenta céntimos.
Cliente: Le doy este billete de veinte euros.
Dependiente: No tengo cambio de veinte. ¿Tiene algo más pequeño?
Cliente: ¿Me lo puede cambiar por dos billetes de diez?
Dependiente: Sí, se lo cambio ahora mismo. Aquí tiene diez y diez.
Cliente: Gracias. Entonces le pago el zumo con uno de diez.
Dependiente: Perfecto. Su cambio son siete euros con cincuenta céntimos.
native: Customer: Good evening. I would like a juice, please.
Shop assistant: Very well. That is two euros and fifty cents.
Customer: I will give you this twenty-euro note.
Shop assistant: I do not have change for twenty. Do you have something smaller?
Customer: Can you change it for me into two ten-euro notes?
Shop assistant: Yes, I will change it for you right now. Here are ten and ten.
Customer: Thank you. Then I will pay for the juice with one of the ten-euro notes.
Shop assistant: Perfect. Your change is seven euros and fifty cents.

5.speaking: You want a small bottle of juice but only have a twenty-euro note. Tell the seller you will pay with it, ask whether they can change it, and accept the change when it is given back. Close by thanking them and confirming the amount.
5.openingLine: Buenas noches. ¿Desea algo más? Tenemos zumo de naranja fresco.
5.partnerRole: Shop assistant at a corner grocery who has few small notes

grammar.focus: Object pronouns go before a conjugated verb, or attach to an infinitive; when le and lo appear together, le becomes se.

examples.es: ¿Me lo puede cambiar?
examples.en: Can you change it for me?

examples.es: Se lo doy ahora mismo.
examples.en: I will give it to you right now.

reading.title: Contar el cambio en la cafetería
target: Sofía: Buenos días. Quiero un sándwich y un café.
Cajera: Son seis euros con cuarenta céntimos.
Sofía: Le doy un billete de diez euros.
Cajera: Aquí tiene el cambio: tres euros con sesenta céntimos.
Sofía: Cuento en voz alta: seis con cuarenta, y el resto es tres con sesenta.
Cajera: Exacto. Diez menos seis con cuarenta es tres con sesenta.
Sofía: ¿Me puede dar el recibo, por favor?
Cajera: Claro. Aquí lo tiene. Gracias por su compra.
native: Sofía: Good morning. I want a sandwich and a coffee.
Cashier: It is six euros and forty cents.
Sofía: I will give you a ten-euro note.
Cashier: Here is your change: three euros and sixty cents.
Sofía: I will count it out loud: six forty, and the rest is three sixty.
Cashier: Exactly. Ten minus six forty is three sixty.
Sofía: Can you give me the receipt, please?
Cashier: Of course. Here you are. Thank you for your purchase.

6.speaking: You buy a sandwich and a coffee that together cost six euros and forty cents, and you pay with a ten-euro note. Work out the change in your head, say it aloud, and ask the cashier to confirm it. Close by saying the change is correct and that you do not need a receipt.
6.openingLine: Buenos días. ¿Qué le sirvo? Tenemos sándwiches frescos y café recién hecho.
6.partnerRole: Cashier at a small bakery who counts change back to the customer

grammar.focus: Cuento and cuenta come from contar, which changes o to ue. Counting money aloud is a natural use of contar.

examples.es: Cuento el cambio en voz alta.
examples.en: I count the change out loud.

examples.es: Ella cuenta las monedas.
examples.en: She counts the coins.
